content.content:
## Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r7` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 1, 2, 2b, 4.1, 4.3 and R3 "Gameplay Designers" (Custom Item Designer + typed ability/event graph + verified component library); research `A-content.md` (items/abilities/projectiles are vanilla-client possible, high AI reliability) and `F-quality-market.md` (verified recipes over free-form code). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** One flag, OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (portal: a build request may get the designer route). Off, nothing is decided or recorded and every build request is byte-identical to before. **Not plan-gated** (owner decision): no plan lookup happens for the designer; any texture / sound / model a design references still goes through the existing asset gates (the texture route needs the top plan, sounds Saka+; without the asset the item keeps its base look / the sound key plays nothing). Installing and keeping are never gated. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the designer lives in `lib/cyrus/designer` and only uses `lib/cyrus/{datapack,engine-core,versions}`); no new tables, no foreign keys; designs are stored in the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "design"`.

**The idea.** Common mechanics (a weapon that marks enemies, a staff with charges and a projectile, a tonic with a timed buff) never need free-form AI Java: the model writes a typed `ItemDesign` (data), Nxeon validates it like code and **compiles** it deterministically into a complete Paper plugin that calls a fixed, reviewed component library. Every number, text and sound key of the graph becomes a `config.yml` parameter, so a later change of cooldown / range / strength / sound changes config.yml only: no regeneration, no model call, not one Java file.

### 1. Files
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/cyrus/designer/spec.ts` | the design IR (Zod): `ItemDesignSchema`, `CAPS`, `BUDGET`, `DESIGN_LIMITS`, curated catalogs, `designFeatures(version)`, `validateDesign` / `validateDesigns` (never throw: `{ ok, design, errors, warnings, checks, budgets }`), `budgetOf`, `walkActions` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/designer.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema, carries every cap), generated |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/components/java.ts`, `components/index.ts` | the verified component library (Java sources + metadata: purpose, families, limits, tests), the per-version `Compat` adapter, `libraryHash()` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/compile.ts` | `compileDesigns(designs, ctx)` -> plugin sources + plugin.yml + config.yml + README, deterministic; parameter collection (`designParams`), `nextConfigVersion` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/params.ts` | the edit path: `describeParameters`, `applyParameterEdits`, `recompileWithEdits`, `diffCompiled`, `planDesignEdit` (deterministic change-request parser) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/simulate.ts` | the TS reference simulator of the graph semantics (`DesignSimulator`, `JavaRandom`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/route.ts` | `decideDesignerRoute`, `matchDesignerWords`, `hasDesigns`, flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDesigns` (portal re-validation + re-compile, `serviceAgreed`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |
| `services/modbuilder/designs.js` | service side: list/snapshot/check designs, asset keys of the workspace, `compileWorkspaceDesigns` |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-spec.js` | GENERATED bundle of the TS validator + compiler (734 KB incl. zod and the id lists) |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-example.json` | the prompt example (= the Void Reaper fixture, namespace `nx_abcd1234`) |
| `scripts/cyrus/build-designer-artifacts.ts` | writes the bundle + JSON Schema (`--check`, `--out-dir DIR`: run through devhost with an out-dir on node-2 and copy back) |
| `scripts/cyrus/designer-golden.ts` | prints the golden compile record (`test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`) |
| `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-designer-real.ts`, `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/` | pure suite, real node-2 runner, the three designs + golden hashes |

Changed: `services/modbuilder/{server.js,prompts.js,textures.js,Dockerfile}`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{request,sync}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/{create,types,client}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/engine-core/store.ts` (asset kind `design`), `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`.

### 2. The design IR (ItemDesign v1)
One file per item, `assets/designs/<id>.json`, at most 6 per mod. `{ schemaVersion: 1, id, base: "minecraft:<item>", name: {text, color?}, lore?, rarity?, glint?, assets?: { model?: "<ns>:<texture name>", sounds?: [keys] }, stats?: { damage + attackSpeed together, durability?, unbreakable? }, passives?: [{effect, amplifier?, slot}], marks?: [{name, durationTicks, maxPerOwner, glow?}], abilities: [0-6], permissions?: [{node, description, default}], recipe?, acquisition?: { loot?: [{table, chance}], drops?: [{entity, chance}] } }`. Unknown keys are refused. The item's identity is `<ns>:<id>` (PersistentDataContainer, never name/lore).
- **Ability** = `{ id, name, trigger, conditions?, actions, cooldownTicks?, charges?: {max, regenTicks}, manualCooldown?, manualCharges?, feedback? }`. Own cooldown and charges are checked before the conditions and spent when the ability fires (unless manual).
- **Triggers**: `right_click` / `sneak_right_click` (`targetRange?`: ray trace for a target entity + aim point), `left_click_hit_entity`, `kill_entity`, `projectile_hit` (`tag` of a `launch_projectile` of the same item), `held_interval` (`periodTicks` >= 10, main hand or inventory), `join`, `death` (fires for the dead player), `item_consume` (edible/drinkable base only), `charge_release` (hold sneak to charge, release by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; `minChargeTicks`, `maxChargeTicks`; actions may `scaleWithCharge`).
- **Conditions** (all must pass, `negate?` on each; a condition about a missing target is always false): `cooldown_ready`, `has_permission` (declared node `<ns>.<node>`), `target_is` (kinds player/hostile/animal/living and/or vanilla entity types), `world_in`, `health_below` / `health_above` (self/target, fraction), `item_identity` (main/off hand holds a design item), `sneaking`, `charges_available`, `random_chance` (java.util.Random seeded with `general.random_seed`), `time_of_day`.
- **Actions**: `damage` (player as the source: PvP and protection plugins apply), `heal`, `potion_effect` (31 curated effects), `knockback`, `pull_to` (self/point), `push_from`, `teleport_short` (self only, safe-spot search), `launch_projectile` (snowball/arrow/small_fireball/wind_charge; tagged, removed after its lifetime, arrows not pickable, fireballs non-incendiary yield 0), `spawn_particles` (28 data-free particles), `play_sound` (namespaced key only), `send_message` / `actionbar` / `title` (plain text + colour, `{player}` `{target}`), `give_item` (vanilla or own design item), `set_cooldown`, `consume_charge`, `apply_mark`, `query_marked` and `query_nearby` (bounded loops: target = each entity), `delayed` (one scheduled step), `branch` (if/then/else). **There is no run_command** and no way to express arbitrary code.
- **Recipe**: the data pack studio's shaped/shapeless shapes (`IngredientSchema` reused: vanilla item, `#tag`, list of items) plus own design items as ingredients (`ExactChoice`); registered by the plugin (a data pack cannot give the result its PDC identity); unlocked for every player on join.

**Caps** (inclusive; the schema refuses outside them, the runtime config loader clamps to the same numbers): cooldown 0-72000 ticks; charges 1-20, regen 20-72000; targetRange 1-32 blocks; held interval 10-1200; charge min 5-200, max 10-400; damage 0-40; heal 0-20; potion 1-1200 ticks, amplifier 0-4; strength 0-3 (blocks/tick), vertical 0-1.5 (velocity also capped at 4); teleport 1-16; projectile speed 0.2-3, lifetime 20-200; particles 1-64, spread 0-4, speed 0-1; volume 0-2, pitch 0.5-2; give 1-64; charge cost 1-5; mark 20-1200 ticks, 1-32 per owner; query_marked radius 1-32, query_nearby radius 1-12, max 1-16; delay 1-100; chance / health fraction / loot chance 0-1; time 0-23999; title fades 0-40, stay 10-200; passive amplifier 0-2; stats damage 1-40, attack speed 0.25-4, durability 1-10000; texts 120 / title 40 / subtitle 60 characters. Structure: 16 actions per list, 8 conditions, 6 abilities, 48 nodes per ability, depth 3, 4 marks, 4 passives, 6 lore lines, 64 KB per file.
**Budget per activation** (static worst case must fit; the `Budget` component enforces it again at runtime, so raising a query's `max` in config.yml cannot exceed it): 64 actions, 32 entity effects, 8 scheduled steps, 512 particles, 3 projectiles. No query inside a query; no delayed / projectile / teleport inside a query. Plugin-wide: 128 live one-shot tasks, 2048 marks.
**Semantic checks** (codes in the tests): banned bases (operator items, spawn eggs, ender pearl/eye, chorus fruit, milk, bundles...), block bases with click abilities, consume on a non-edible base, damage/attackSpeed pair, unresolved abilities/marks/items/projectile tags/permissions, reserved permission nodes, vanilla ids per exact version (items, entity types, loot tables, tags), foreign namespaces, missing target for the trigger, ambiguous sneak triggers, harmful/instant passives, recipe pattern/key, self-ingredient, plugin command name = a vanilla command, two ids mapping to one Java class. Warnings: item model on 1.21.1, unresolved asset keys, vanilla sound keys (not checked against the game).
**Optional-field defaults**: knockback lift 0.35, pull 0.25, push 0.35, amplifier 0, projectile lifetime 100, particle spread 0.3 / speed 0.02, volume 1, pitch 1, title 10/40/10 ticks, give count 1, charge cost 1, passive amplifier 0.

### 3. Verified component library (`lib/cyrus/designer/components`)
Fixed Java, rendered into `<pkg>.designer`: `Trigger`, `Budget`, `Activation`, `ItemIdentity` (PDC `<ns>:item`), `Cooldowns` (per player + ability, server ticks), `Charges` (lazy regeneration, no task), `Marks` (per-owner cap with oldest replaced, plugin-wide cap, cleanup on expiry / target death / owner quit or death / disable), `Tasks` (Paper main-thread scheduler only, tracked, capped, all cancelled on disable; timers restarted on reload), `DesignConfig` (jar defaults, clamping, migration hook), `Checks`, `Targets` (ray trace, nearby sphere, nearest first, never the player, no armor stands, players only on request), `Effects` (every action), `Ability` (the fixed activation protocol: re-entry guard -> own cooldown -> own charges -> conditions -> start cooldown / spend charge -> actions), `DesignItem`, `Designer` (the hub: owns all state, drops a player's state on quit and death), `DesignListener` (the safe listener base), `DesignCommand`, and the per-version `Compat`. Each component's metadata lists its purpose, families (1.21 and 26), limits and tests.
- **Listener rules**: observation handlers run at MONITOR and never change or cancel an event; they skip events another plugin cancelled (`ignoreCancelled`), except `PlayerInteractEvent`, which Bukkit delivers already "cancelled" for right-clicks in the air: there the item-use result is checked instead (DENY = another plugin blocked it). The two handlers that ADD items (loot tables via `LootGenerateEvent`, mob drops) run at NORMAL. Main hand only; one click activation per player per tick. The re-entry guard means effects of an activation (its damage, a kill it causes) never trigger abilities again.
- **Scheduling**: Paper-only (`BukkitScheduler`, main thread). No Folia region schedulers and plugin.yml does not claim `folia-supported`; `designFeatures(v).scheduling` is `"paper"` for every registry version (the registry has no Folia lane).
- **Commands** (plugin.yml, no Brigadier): `/<plugin lowercase> give <item> [player] [count]` (`<ns>.give`), `list` and `params [item]` (`<ns>.command`), `reload` (`<ns>.reload`); all operators by default; console can use all (give needs a player name there).
- **Config migration hook**: config.yml carries `config_version` and `# designer-values: <hash>`. When the jar's `config_version` is newer than the file on the server (the design's parameters were edited in Cyrus), every value under `items.` is reset to the jar's new default (Cyrus is the source of truth for designer values), the old file is kept as `config.yml.bak-v<N>`, `general.` is kept. A recompile with unchanged values keeps `config_version`.

### 4. Compiler (`compile.ts`)
`compileDesigns(designs, { version, namespace, pluginName, customHooks?, previousConfig?, configVersion?, assets? })` -> `{ files [{path, content, sha256, role}], readme, hash, params, pkg, mainClass, command, configVersion, designerValuesHash, modelsApplied, notes, javacVerified, libraryHash }`. Package `dev.nxeon.plugins.<lowercase name>`; main class; `items/<Item>Item.java` (ItemStack: `itemName`, lore, rarity, glint, item model through `Compat`, attribute modifiers keyed in the namespace, max damage + stack size 1, PDC identity; recipe; passives every 40 ticks; loot/drops); `abilities/<Item><Ability>.java` (straight-line Java: one field per parameter loaded by `load()` through `DesignConfig`, `check()` with the conditions, `run()` with the actions, budget checks before every action, `describe()` for `/params`). Items are sorted by id, so file order does not change the output. Deterministic: same designs + context = same bytes (golden hashes for all six versions in `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`).
**Per-version differences** (from the javap-verified API sheets + failure rules): `Attribute.GENERIC_ATTACK_DAMAGE/ATTACK_SPEED/MAX_HEALTH` on 1.21.1 (enum), unprefixed from 1.21.3 (registry interface; `designFeatures` uses 1.21.3, the registry's first plain version is 1.21.4); `ItemMeta#setItemModel` from 1.21.4 (registry capability `itemModelDefinitions`): on 1.21.1 the item keeps its base look and the README says so; `api-version` = the exact version; JDK release 21 / 25 from the registry. Everything else is the same source on all versions (each component's text is identical across versions; a test checks it). With `assets.models` given, an item model the mod does not have is left out (the item keeps its base look instead of the missing-model checkerboard).

### 5. Edit without regenerating (`params.ts`)
Every graph value is a parameter at a stable config path: `items.<item>.abilities.<ability>.cooldown_ticks`, `.charges.max|regen_ticks`, `.trigger.target_range|period_ticks|min_charge_ticks|max_charge_ticks`, `.<node>.<field>` with node paths `a<i>` (actions), `.n<j>` (inside query/delayed), `.then<j>` / `.else<j>`, `c<i>` / `.if<j>` (conditions); item level `items.<item>.marks.<name>.*`, `.passives.p<i>.amplifier`, `.loot.l<i>.chance`, `.drops.d<i>.chance`. Structure stays code: kinds, effects, particles, targets, stats, recipe, base.
- `applyParameterEdits(designs, [{path, value}])` checks each value against the parameter's caps; `recompileWithEdits(previous, edits, ctx)` recompiles against the previous config.yml and returns the diff.
- **Demonstration (test + real run)**: editing the Void Pull cooldown 160 -> 100, target range 24 -> 30, query radius 16 -> 20, pull strength 1.2 -> 2.0 and its sound -> `minecraft:entity.warden.sonic_boom` changes exactly ONE source file (`src/main/resources/config.yml`, `config_version` 1 -> 2) plus the README text; all 27 Java files are byte-identical, and in the rebuilt jar the only differing entry is `config.yml` (every .class identical, on 1.21.11 and 26.2). A structural change (a particle) changes exactly that ability's Java file and the config labels.
- `planDesignEdit(text, designs)`: a deterministic parser for change requests that only tweak parameters ("set the void pull cooldown to 5 seconds and the pull strength to 2", "change the void pull sound to nx_x:void_reaper.boom", "set the storm bolt cooldown to 40 ticks, storm bolt charges to 5"). Seconds are the default unit for ticks; `%` and hearts convert. A clause without a name inherits the previous clause's item/ability. Anything structural ("add", "instead", "make it shoot..."), unreadable or ambiguous (two items with a sound) returns `{ kind: "model" }` with the candidates. It is a pure API: the host can apply the edits with `recompileWithEdits` and skip the model; **not wired into `create.ts`** (decision below).

### 6. Reference simulator (`simulate.ts`)
A TS twin of the runtime: same activation protocol, cooldowns in ticks, lazy charges, marks (per-owner eviction order, expiry, death cleanup), the click / sneak / charge dispatch, the static + runtime budget, the re-entry guard (a kill caused by the activation logs `kill_trigger_suppressed`), delayed steps (dropped when the player left), held_interval timers, clamped config overrides (`config` option), and `JavaRandom` (a port of java.util.Random: the same seed gives the same `random_chance` sequence as the plugin; checked against real Java 21 on node-2). It logs effects (damage/heal/potions/velocity vectors/particles/sounds/texts/marks/branches); physics, real ray tracing, protection plugins and clients are NOT simulated.

### 7. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts` like the data pack route): with the flag on, a request with an item word (sword, staff, wand, tonic, potion, relic, bow, ...) AND an ability word (cooldown, right-click, charge, mark, pull, dash, teleport, projectile, buff, heal, on hit, on kill, passive, ...), `assets: ["design"]`, or a base build that has designs -> `service.assets.design = true` + the project namespace (a project is created if needed), `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.designer = { route, matched, limits }`. An unsupported version (26.3) gets a notice and no route.
- **Service**: `assets.design` parsed (non-boolean = 400; off with a note on unsupported versions); the `ITEM DESIGNER` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text; namespace in the user turn); allow-list `assets/designs/<id>.json`; a change build without the route keeps the base's designs byte for byte. Each round, BEFORE validate(): `designRound` validates every design with the generated bundle (+ the workspace's texture/sound keys); hard problems go back as a `design` repair (shared `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`); afterwards failing designs are dropped (customer-visible) and the rest re-checked; the valid ones are COMPILED into the workspace: generated sources replace every Java file outside `<pkg>.custom` and the plugin.yml / config.yml (free-form Java only in `custom/`, entry `CustomHooks.enable(JavaPlugin)` / `disable()`, wired into the main class when present). No valid design = the build fails clearly (never a half mod). Then the normal validate / precheck / javac / strict scan run on the generated code. `assetResult.designs` + `designCompile` (hash, config_version, settings, README, notes) + `designPromptVersion` `mb-design-2026-10-10.1`; `rec.config` lists the settings when the model's summary has none; designer builds are never deduped; `/health` lists `design`. The image needs `designer-spec.js`, `designs.js`, `designer-example.json` (Dockerfile updated).
- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `designer/sync.ts`): every returned design is re-validated and the whole mod re-compiled with the TypeScript compiler (the service's `configVersion`, `customHooks` and applied models reproduced); `serviceAgreed` = the hashes match; one manifest row `assets/designs/<id>.json` (role `asset`) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` (`kind design`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.item-design+json`, provenance = spec, compiler, library hash, compile hash, config_version, serviceAgreed, javacVerified) per design; `MbAssets.designs`. Idempotent like the other assets.

### 8. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts` 75/75 (every one of the 39 caps at min/max accepted and just outside refused; 30+ semantic error codes; static budgets; JSON Schema current; components present + documented; golden hashes on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11/26.1.2/26.2 and order independence; per-version differences; generated code free of reflection/threads/network/commands and clean under the strict source rules and the service's precheck rules for every version; config.yml/plugin.yml/README; custom hooks; unresolved models; parameter edits touch only config.yml; structural edit touches one Java file; edit refusals; the change-request parser; simulator scenarios for all three designs + permissions/negate/re-entry/runtime budget/clamping + held_interval/join/death; JavaRandom; TS == generated JS on fixtures + broken corpus for 3 versions; artifacts current; prompt section; routing; not-plan-gated request; portal sync). `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` 24/24 (4 new: designer build compiles the design into the workspace with the model's main + plugin.yml replaced and custom hooks kept, service hash == TypeScript; an out-of-cap value -> one design repair -> ships; a design that keeps failing -> dropped -> clear failure; not routed -> file removed, malformed flag 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite on the final code: 1279/1279 (an earlier run failed the image COPY test until the Dockerfile listed the new files, plus the known load-flaky `cyrus-admin.test.ts`, which passes alone). `tsc` clean.
- RAN REAL on node-2 (`devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-designer-real.ts --out ...`; raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/designer-r3-flights-2026-10-10.json`), one flight at a time:

| Lane | javac (27 sources, -Xlint:deprecation,removal) | Catalog (28 particles, 31 effects, 25 bases, 4 projectiles) | Jar | Strict scan | Test Flight | Edit jar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.11 / JDK 21.0.12 / Paper b132 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings (bytecode + source) | passed 6/6, boot 17.5 s, 857 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |
| 26.2 / JDK 25.0.4 / Paper b133 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings | passed 6/6, boot 13.8 s, 782 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |

  RCON evidence per flight: `plugins` lists VoidArsenal; `help voidarsenal` shows the plugin.yml command; `/voidarsenal` lists the three items; `/voidarsenal list` = `identity=ok`, the right material, ability count and `recipe=registered` for all three (so every ItemStack was built at runtime: names, lore, rarity, glint, item model, attribute modifiers, max damage, PDC); `give` from the console -> usage, to an offline player -> "not online", unknown item -> refused; `params` shows the defaults; an out-of-range config.yml (strength 99, cooldown -5, a bad sound key) + `/voidarsenal reload` -> clamped to 3.0 / 0 / the default key (logged as WARN, never an error); a config.yml with `config_version: 0` -> "migrated from version 0 to 1 ... backup config.yml.bak-v0" and the defaults back; on disk: config.yml written by the plugin and the backup present; no ERROR line from the plugin (4 sandbox no-internet lines, ignored by Test Flight). The edit flight boots the parameter-edited jar over the OLD config.yml: the plugin migrates it to `config_version 2` and `/params` shows cooldown 100, range 30, strength 2.0, the new sound. java.util.Random on JDK 21 printed the same sequences the simulator test asserts. Afterwards: empty `runs/`, no marker process.
- **NOT RUN**: no real Minecraft client and no bot: **gameplay behaviour was not verified in a game** (clicks, hits, marks, pulls, projectiles, particles, sounds, potions, teleports, recipes in a crafting grid, loot injection, passives); the simulator covers the logic, not the game. javac was not run for 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 26.1.2 (no resolved classpath on the build host): those sources follow the API sheets and the failure rules (`javacVerified: false` in every compile result); in particular the 1.21.1 `GENERIC_` Compat variant is unverified by javac. No real model build (fake CLI only, no paid AI): how well a real model writes designs is unmeasured. No customer server, no production DB, no migration, no deploy.

### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- One ItemDesign per file; at most 6 items per mod; the designer owns the main class, plugin.yml and config.yml; free-form Java only in `<pkg>.custom` (CustomHooks); custom code cannot add commands (plugin.yml is generated).
- Every numeric/text/sound value is a config parameter (auto paths), instead of asking the model to name parameters; structure stays code. Parameter defaults live only in the jar's config.yml (Java has the caps, not the values), which is why edits never touch Java.
- Designer values are reset on a `config_version` bump (Cyrus is the source of truth), with a backup; hand edits of designer values survive reloads but not a Cyrus edit of the same mod.
- `charge_release` = hold sneak to charge (no client mod, no experimental data components), released by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; an item cannot have both sneak_right_click and a right-click release.
- Item-consume abilities run at MONITOR, so a cooldown does not stop the item being eaten (no refund).
- Stats (damage, attack speed, durability) and the recipe are code, baked into items when they are created (changing them later does not alter items players already hold).
- Unresolved own-namespace item models are left out of the jar; unresolved sound keys are only warnings.
- No query nesting and no delayed/projectile/teleport inside a query (bounded fan-out); damage uses the player as the source so PvP/protection plugins decide; teleport is self-only.
- `planDesignEdit` is exposed as a pure API and NOT wired into the build request: skipping the model for a change changes billing/revision semantics (a "build" without the service) and needs an owner decision and a service endpoint that rebuilds from edited designs.
- Designer builds that end with no valid design FAIL instead of falling back to free-form Java (no half mods, no surprise cost).

### 10. Owner actions (nothing needed to merge)
1. Decide whether to switch `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (portal) after a small paid eval of real model-written designs (not run).
2. Rebuild the build-service image with `designs.js`, `designer-spec.js`, `designer-example.json` (VM 88001 untouched).
3. Decide whether parameter-only change requests should skip the model (wire `planDesignEdit` + a service rebuild endpoint) and how they are billed.
4. A real-client test day (T): Void Reaper mark + charged pull, Storm Staff charges + impact, Vigor Tonic buff, recipes, on 1.21.11 and 26.x.
5. Optional: resolve Paper classpaths for 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/26.1.2 on node-2 so those lanes are javac-verified too.
6. Cleanup when no longer needed: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-r7-designer` (small; the real runner deletes its run dirs).

content.thinking:
I'm noting version differences: 26.2 introduces `transformation` across several model types, 1.21.11 adds an `on_shelf` display context missing from 1.21.4, and ClientItem properties expand from just `hand_animation_on_swap` in 1.21.4 to also include `oversized_in_gui` and `swap_animation_scale` in 1.21.11. I'm also flagging that shields and tridents need special handling in 26.2.

I'm turning to the custom model data component, tracing how it evolved from `floats`/`flags`/`strings`/`colors` lists in 1.21.4 into Paper's `CustomModelDataComponent` ItemMeta API and the newer experimental `DataComponentTypes.CUSTOM_MODEL_DATA` builder pattern, which matters for how the designer tool should construct these components.

For gun aiming states, I'm considering whether the "using" visual could piggyback on the `minecraft:consumable` component's `using_item` condition, but that risks the item actually completing consumption after `consume_seconds`. Setting `consume_seconds` to something enormous like 3600 so it never finishes seems like a workaround, and I want to check Paper's `Consumable` data component API for how to configure that cleanly.

One reliable safeguard is canceling `PlayerItemConsumeEvent` server-side so the item never actually gets consumed even if the duration runs out, which keeps the "using" animation active purely for aiming purposes without any risk of item loss.

Thinking through animation choices, I'm weighing "bow" versus "crossbow" for the held pose — crossbow's two-arm forward stance in vanilla is tied to the charging animation and a separate ArmPose rather than the generic use animation, so it may not render that way outside of actual crossbow items, while "bow" might give a closer approximation for a gun-aiming pose.

I also note that the spyglass zoom overlay is hardcoded to check if the item is actually `minecraft:spyglass`, so just using the spyglass use-animation won't trigger scoping on a custom item. I should document the movement slowdown that happens while using items as expected vanilla behavior, and for a custom bow-type item, base it on `minecraft:bow` with a custom item model while setting up the using_item/use animation properties in its definition.

Next I want to check how bow pull duration scaling and thresholds work versus vanilla, then dig into display.ts, pack.ts, held.ts, and related texture/designer files to understand handheld display transforms and model compilation.

# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres

59-## Items and recipes
60-- `ItemStack.of(Material.DIAMOND, 5)` or `new ItemStack(mat, n)`. `item.editMeta(meta -> { meta.displayName(Component.text("Super", NamedTextColor.GOLD).decoration(TextDecoration.ITALIC, false)); meta.lore(List.of(Component.text("..."))); meta.setUnbreakable(true); meta.addItemFlags(ItemFlag.HIDE_ENCHANTS); meta.setEnchantmentGlintOverride(true); })`. getItemMeta() is null for AIR. Hand: player.getInventory().getItemInMainHand() (getItemInHand is deprecated); setHelmet(item).
61:- 1.21.4 also has ItemMeta.customName(Component), setItemModel(NamespacedKey), setEquippable, setUseCooldown, setGlider and io.papermc.paper.datacomponent.DataComponentTypes (experimental: prefer ItemMeta).
62-- give items: `player.getInventory().addItem(item)` returns leftovers (HashMap) to drop with world.dropItemNaturally. `player.give(items)` also exists.
63-- Recipes: `ShapedRecipe r = new ShapedRecipe(new NamespacedKey(plugin, "super_pickaxe"), result); r.shape("DDD", " S ", " S "); r.setIngredient('D', Material.DIAMOND_BLOCK); r.setIngredient('S', Material.STICK); Bukkit.addRecipe(r);` unlock with player.discoverRecipe(key); Bukkit.removeRecipe(key) in onDisable. ShapedRecipe(ItemStack) without a key is deprecated.
64-
65-## Boss bars and scoreboards
66-- Adventure boss bar: `BossBar bar = BossBar.bossBar(Component.text("Boss"), 1.0f, BossBar.Color.RED, BossBar.Overlay.PROGRESS); player.showBossBar(bar); bar.progress(f); player.hideBossBar(bar);` progress must stay within 0..1 (clamp it). Colors PINK BLUE RED GREEN YELLOW PURPLE WHITE; overlays PROGRESS, NOTCHED_6/10/12/20. Hide it from everyone when done and in onDisable.
67-- Sidebar: `Scoreboard sb = Bukkit.getScoreboardManager().getNewScoreboard(); Objective o = sb.registerNewObjective("side", Criteria.DUMMY, Component.text("Title")); o.setDisplaySlot(DisplaySlot.SIDEBAR); o.numberFormat(NumberFormat.blank()); o.getScore("line").setScore(3); player.setScoreboard(sb);` (NumberFormat is io.papermc.paper.scoreboard.numbers.NumberFormat). The registerNewObjective overloads that take a criteria String are deprecated. Score entries must be unique strings (max 15 lines); keep one scoreboard per player and update scores instead of recreating it every tick; reset changed lines with sb.resetScores(entry).

I'm worried the naive tree construction duplicates the "rest" branch for every condition in a conjunction, so nesting multiple multi-condition states could blow up exponentially even with small caps like 8 states and 2 conditions each. Each layer is structured so there's no duplication: conditions and selects just fall through to the next layer as their "else" case, and range entries stack similarly.

I'm reasoning through validation rules too, like disallowing both a plain "using" state and pull stages simultaneously, so the state tree stays compact — roughly proportional to the number of states plus layers rather than exploding combinatorially. Writing schema definition...

I'm continuing to lay out validation constraints — crossbow-specific pull sources, mutual exclusivity between using/pull, stage ordering for pull and damage, context disjointness across states, uniqueness of ids and texture names matching the same regex as TextureSpec. I also need a separate warning for designs that define states but have no assets.model (`states_without_model`), and the service should cross-check that state mode values actually match flags defined in the referenced item model spec.

For flag indexing, the real risk is that the design's declared flag order might not match the item model spec's declaration order, since indexes are assigned by position. To avoid mismatches, I'll have the system prefer an index map built from the compile context's item model spec (`ctx.assets.itemModels[model].flags`) when available, falling back to the design's own declaration order otherwise -- implemented through the CompileContext.

Beyond that, I need to confirm the gun design uses a consumable-style "using" state for aiming, and that the bow design can simply extend minecraft:bow with a custom item_model, relying on vanilla pull/use_duration behavior without extra code -- just need to verify the designer permits a bow base.

Now I'm starting the ModelStates Java class, setting up imports for Paper's data component API, consumable item use animations, and player item consume events.

I'm defining a Rule record that captures item, ability, cooldown state, display mode, and flag values, plus setting up the core fields for tracking the designer reference, rule list, and active item sets.

Still writing tick logic...

Checking rule activation by ability state: cooldown, charges remaining, or charging status tied to the player's held item, with a note that no-charges logic needs a guard since zero max charges would always evaluate as "no charges."

Now I'm writing a helper that applies a custom_model_data component to an item stack, setting its mode string and flags only if they differ from the current values, returning whether a change occurred. I'm noting that an empty mode/flags combination leaves an empty component on the item, which should be harmless since vanilla falls back gracefully, but I want to double check that assumption.

This raises a stacking and crafting concern: items with set components (even empty ones) differ structurally from freshly created items, so they won't stack together, and recipes using ExactChoice ingredient matching could fail to recognize a modified item as equivalent to a vanilla one. To avoid this, I'm considering removing the component entirely when mode is null and all flags are false, checking whether passing null to the setter actually clears it in CraftMetaItem's implementation.

I'm planning a self-check routine that builds each item, applies every mode and flag combination, reads back the resulting component strings, and verifies clearing works correctly by comparing states before and after.

Writing consumable component code...

I'm using a silent placeholder sound key for the consumable animation, wondering whether Paper validates it against the registry or just wraps it as a direct holder if unregistered.

I should also handle the consume event for aim items by cancelling it when the full duration elapses, since Paper will resend inventory state after cancellation. The use duration translates to about an hour of max hold time at 20 ticks per second, which seems fine since the use-duration property just increments while aiming, and I need to note that consuming items like this slows player movement similar to drawing a bow — plus checking when eat particle/sound thresholds trigger during that long window.

Now I'm thinking through the interaction model for a gun-type ability: does right-click both begin aiming and fire, or are these separate triggers? The client only sends a single use-item packet on press rather than continuously while held, so I need to decide whether firing happens per-click or is tied to the aim state, leaning toward right-click triggering both the aim start and the fire action for the gun template design.

This leads naturally into mapping out the full mode system: reload triggered by sneak-right-click with its own cooldown that drives a "reloading" display mode, an "empty" mode when the fire ability runs out of charges (treating charges as ammo/magazine capacity), and a "charging" mode for staff-type weapons tied to a charge-release trigger. I'm also noting that chargeStart is accessible within the designer package, and that the spec validation needs to confirm every ability referenced in a mode actually exists in the design.

Each mode has its own prerequisite: no_charges needs the ability to track charges, charging needs a charge_release trigger, and cooldown needs either a positive cooldown duration or a manual cooldown flag. For aim mode, I need to block it on bases where the item's default use behavior would conflict — bows, crossbows, tridents, shields, spyglasses, goat horns, brushes, fishing rods, and edible items — since letting a consumable override those would break their native functionality, so I'm flagging this as an `aim_base` validation error. content.thinking:
I'm sketching a plan for the studio preview module - building a pure function that renders context scenes (gui/ground/fixed/head) as orthographic projections through the transform, with backdrop elements like slot frames, ground shadows, and outline borders, while reusing the held-item scene logic for first/third person views.

For the UI, I'm figuring out how to wire itemModels into ProjectAssetsView and TextureStudio, then deciding how to extend the LivePreview panel so it can switch between the six display contexts (hotbar, dropped, first-person, third-person, item frame, head) plus a state scrubber, while trying to keep the existing tab layout intact so I don't break prior expectations.

I need to work out where the state scrubber's texture comes from, matching the current texture to its item model spec or falling back to a derived default based on grip kind, so textures without explicit item model specs still render using the existing handheld/gun display logic.

For rendering the gui, ground, and fixed contexts, I'm planning simplified orthographic approximations: gui shows a flat front-facing sprite in a slot square, ground shows a scaled-down 3/4 perspective view with bobbing/rotation and a shadow ellipse, and fixed represents the item-frame view.

For fixed, I need to account for the vanilla transform's 180° Y rotation plus the item frame renderer's own counter-rotation, since in-game the item isn't actually mirrored — the frame renderer applies its own 180° Y rotation that cancels it out, so I should replicate both to get the correct unmirrored appearance.

For the head slot, I'm drawing a skin-colored head cube from a 3/4 front angle with the item positioned above and slightly in front per the vanilla transform values.

My implementation plan is a single generic 3D orthographic projector: transform model points by the display transform into world space, then apply a context-specific yaw/pitch view rotation and project to 2D, with a backdrop for context.

I decide to write a self-contained slab builder in preview.ts rather than extracting shared logic from held.ts, to avoid risking existing behavior. Writing preview module types and context definitions...

I'm defining per-context view angles for gui, ground, fixed, and head perspectives, then working out how the display transform converts to render units and how item frames apply extra rotation and translation before rendering.

For fixed context, since vanilla's generated.json includes a 180° Y rotation because the frame renders the item from behind, I'm matching that by flipping the x-axis in screen projection to show the correct face, then setting up the camera math: yaw around Y, pitch around X, with screen x mapped directly and y inverted.

For visibility, I'll draw both front and back faces for each texel as quads sorted by depth, painter's-algorithm style, darkening the back face — good enough for a thin slab. For backdrops, I need a fixed-size slot square behind GUI items sized to match the vanilla 18x18px slot, built in model space using identity transform since it's screen-locked rather than tied to the item's rotation.

Now I'm working through the positioning for ground shadows — a circular ellipse placed slightly below the item's lowest point — and figuring out item-frame borders, while untangling the depth/camera-space conventions so backdrops render correctly relative to the rotated item.

For the head slot, I'm tracing how the head-worn item's translation maps relative to the neck pivot: the head cube spans roughly 8px, and the item's translation offset (0,13,7) would place it well above the head top, so I need to double-check whether that's actually correct for how vanilla renders helmets.

Then I recall the actual mechanism: CustomHeadLayer applies its own transform to head-slot items — translating down by a quarter block, flipping 180 degrees, and scaling by 0.625 with inverted y/z — so I'm working out how that composite transform converts the item's px coordinates into the final head-relative position.

Working through the math, the translation puts the item about 4px above the head top, while the 180° Y rotation and z-flip determine whether it sits forward or behind depending on facing direction. I'm trying to approximate the final world-space transform combining the flip and rotation into one function.

The head cube spans roughly ±4px in x and z and 0-8px in y, rendered with the brand violet skin, and the camera view for the head preview uses a yaw of -35 and pitch of 15 for a 3/4 front angle. Now I'm planning to write preview.ts and make a minimal change to held.ts to add an optional override parameter.

## Cyrus item model states (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r10` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN "Item model states and display contexts": one custom item can look different per display context (hotbar slot, dropped, item frame, head, first / third person hands) and switch looks by state (a bow idle vs pulled back in 3 stages, a gun idle / aiming / reloading, a staff charging). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** One flag, OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES=1` (portal: a texture build may also get item model states). Off, nothing is decided or recorded and every build request is byte-identical to before. **Gates**: item model states are part of the TEXTURE asset (top plan `all`); the router only adds them when the plan already allowed textures. The designer side (`ItemDesign.states`) follows the designer (not plan-gated); without the texture asset the item simply keeps one look. Keeping / installing is never gated. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel` only uses `lib/cyrus/{textures,versions,datapack,studios}`), no new tables (asset rows `CyrusProjectAsset.kind = "itemmodel"`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.item-model+json`).

### 1. Verified vanilla format (2026-10-10)
Sources: the vanilla asset mirror github.com/InventivetalentDev/minecraft-assets (branches 1.21.4, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.1.2, 26.2; sparse clone of `assets/minecraft/items` + `models/item`) and the vanilla CLIENT jars from Mojang's piston-meta (1.21.4 and 1.21.11 with the official client mappings, 26.2 unobfuscated; sha1-verified; constant pools read in a scratch dir; nothing committed except hashes). Paper side: `javap` on node-2 against paper-api 1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT and 26.2.build.133-stable.
- **Definition node types** (`ItemModels`): `minecraft:model`, `range_dispatch`, `special`, `composite`, `select`, `condition`, `empty`, plus `bundle/selected_item` (same on 1.21.4 / 1.21.11 / 26.2). Fields: condition `property`, `on_true`, `on_false`; select `property`, `cases[{when, model}]` (`when` = a value or a list), `fallback`; range_dispatch `property`, `scale`, `entries[{threshold, model}]`, `fallback` (the entry with the highest threshold <= value x scale wins); composite `models`; model `model`, `tints`. **26.x adds an optional `transformation` field** to condition / select / range_dispatch / composite / model (vanilla 26.2 uses it on the special shield and trident models: scale [1,-1,-1]); Cyrus does not emit it. Top-level item fields: `hand_animation_on_swap` (1.21.4+); `oversized_in_gui`, `swap_animation_scale` (1.21.11+, not used).
- **Condition properties**: `custom_model_data` (field `index`, reads flags[index]), `using_item`, `broken`, `damaged`, `has_component`, `bundle/has_selected_item`, `selected`, `carried`, `extended_view`, `keybind_down`, `view_entity`. **Select**: `custom_model_data` (`index`, strings[index]), `main_hand`, `charge_type`, `trim_material`, `block_state`, `display_context`, `local_time`, `context_entity_type`, `context_dimension` (+ `component` on 1.21.11+). **Range**: `custom_model_data` (`index`, floats), `bundle/fullness`, `damage` (`normalize`), `cooldown`, `time`, `compass`, `crossbow/pull`, `use_cycle`, `use_duration` (`remaining`), `count`.
- **Display contexts** (`ItemDisplayContext`): none, thirdperson_lefthand, thirdperson_righthand, firstperson_lefthand, firstperson_righthand, head, gui, ground, fixed; **`on_shelf` from 1.21.9** (present in 1.21.11 and 26.2, absent in 1.21.4 and 1.21.8). Transform caps (`ItemTransform` deserializer constants): translation x 0.0625 clamped to +-5 blocks (= +-80 in model units), scale clamped to +-4, rotation not clamped.
- **Vanilla bow** (`items/bow.json`, byte-identical on 1.21.4 / 1.21.11 / 26.2, sha256 `65ccad78...`): condition `minecraft:using_item` -> on_true range_dispatch `minecraft:use_duration` scale `0.05`, entries `bow_pulling_1` at `0.65`, `bow_pulling_2` at `0.9`, fallback `bow_pulling_0`; on_false `item/bow`. Cyrus's emitter given the vanilla states produces the SAME BYTES (test).
- **Vanilla crossbow**: 1.21.4 = condition using_item { on_true range_dispatch `minecraft:crossbow/pull` entries 0.58 / 1.0 fallback pulling_0; on_false select `minecraft:charge_type` cases `arrow` / `rocket` fallback crossbow }. **1.21.11 and 26.2 swap the two outer layers** (select charge_type outermost, condition using_item in its fallback). Cyrus's order equals 1.21.11 / 26.2 by canonical hash; the 1.21.4 order is the swap (canonical hash checked) and the evaluator shows both pick the same model for every reachable input (a charged crossbow is never "used").
- **Model display defaults**: `item/generated` ground [0,0,0]/[0,2,0]/0.5, head [0,180,0]/[0,13,7]/1, thirdperson_righthand [0,0,0]/[0,3,1]/0.55, firstperson_righthand [0,-90,25]/[1.13,3.2,1.13]/0.68, fixed [0,180,0]/-/1; `item/handheld` the four hands as before; `item/bow` thirdperson_righthand [-80,260,-40]/[-1,-2,2.5]/0.9, lefthand [-80,-280,40], firstperson [0,-90,25] / [0,90,-25]; `item/crossbow` thirdperson [-90,0,-60] / [-90,0,30] at [2,0.1,-3]/0.9, firstperson [-90,0,-55] / [-90,0,35]. generated / handheld / bow / crossbow / bow_pulling_* / crossbow_pulling_* are identical (canonical) on 1.21.4, 1.21.11 and 26.2.
- **Components** (`CustomModelData` codec): `floats`, `flags`, `strings`, `colors`. `Consumable`: `consume_seconds`, `animation`, `sound`, `has_consume_particles`, `on_consume_effects`. `ItemUseAnimation`: 1.21.4 none/eat/drink/block/bow/spear/crossbow/spyglass/toot_horn/brush/bundle; 26.2 adds `trident` (and keeps `spear` for the new spear): Cyrus only offers bow / crossbow / spyglass / none.
- **Paper API** (javap, both lanes): `ItemMeta#getCustomModelDataComponent / setCustomModelDataComponent / hasCustomModelDataComponent / getAsComponentString`, `CustomModelDataComponent#get/setFlags(List<Boolean>) / get/setStrings(List<String>)` (stable Bukkit API); `DataComponentTypes.CONSUMABLE`, `Consumable.consumable()` builder (`consumeSeconds(float)`, `animation`, `sound(Key)`, `hasConsumeParticles`), `ItemUseAnimation.{NONE,BOW,CROSSBOW,SPYGLASS,...}`, `ItemStack#setData/hasData`. `DataComponentTypes` is `@ApiStatus.Experimental` on 1.21.11 and `@MinecraftVersionDependent` (not experimental) on 26.2; the registry's `dataComponentsStable` capability is only on 26.3 (left unchanged; worth re-checking).

### 2. ItemModelSpec v1 (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel/spec.ts`, `itemmodel.v1.schema.json`)
One file per stateful item, `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`, at most 12 per mod, 16 KB each: `{ schemaVersion: 1, name, category, display?, states?: [{ id, label?, texture, when, display? }], handAnimationOnSwap? }`. `name` = the idle texture's name = the item model key (`<ns>:<name>`, what `setItemModel` / the design's `assets.model` already point at). Categories (display defaults, `display.ts`): sword / tool / wand = vanilla handheld, bow = vanilla bow, crossbow = vanilla crossbow, flat / shield = vanilla generated, gun = the existing Cyrus handgun rotations re-gripped on the idle pixels. `display` overrides any context and field (owner/studio), per state too; all 8 contexts are always written explicitly (a missing left hand = the right hand, like the deserializer).
**Conditions** (closed set; layer order outermost first, first match wins): `broken` -> `damage {from}` (range_dispatch damage, normalised) -> `mode {value}` (select custom_model_data strings[0]) -> `flag {name}` (condition custom_model_data flags[i], i = declaration order) -> `charged {charge}` (crossbow only) -> `using` | `pull {from, source?}` (using_item + range_dispatch use_duration scale 0.05, or crossbow/pull) -> `selected` -> `context {contexts}` (select display_context) -> idle. **Caps**: 8 states, 9 textures, 4 pull stages (exactly one from 0), 6 modes, 4 flags, 4 damage stages, 3 context states, rotation +-360, translation +-80, scale +-4, pull from 0-100. Codes: reserved_id, dup_state, using_and_pull, pull_no_start, pull_mixed, crossbow_only, crossbow_range, dup_mode/flag/damage/charged/using/selected/broken, too_many_*, context_overlap, context_all, texture_unknown, version, too_big; warning use_needs_usable_base. **Versions**: 1.21.4+ (registry `itemModelDefinitions`); 1.21.1 refused with the registry's message. **The legacy predicate / overrides emitter for 1.21.1 is OUT of scope.**

### 3. Generator + pack (`emit.ts`, `templates.ts`, `lib/cyrus/textures/pack.ts`)
`emitItemModel(spec, {namespace, version, textures?, idle?})` -> `assets/<ns>/items/<name>.json` (vanilla key order: type first, then alphabetical; 2-space JSON), `models/item/<name>.json` (idle) and `models/item/<name>/<state>.json` (parent `minecraft:item/generated`, `layer0` = the state's texture, full display). `hand_animation_on_swap: false` when plugin-set states exist (a custom_model_data change would bob the hand). Same bytes on every version family (golden hashes for bow / gun / sword / staff on 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2). `buildPack({..., itemModels})`: textures covered by a spec get the spec's files instead of the flat default; **no specs = byte-identical packs** (sha1 compared with pack.ts at 5aa6fe5e52). `evalNode` / `resolveState` / `inputForState`: a TS evaluator of definitions (ours or vanilla's) for tests and the studio. Templates: bow (idle + pulling_0/1/2 at 0 / 0.65 / 0.9), gun (reloading mode > aiming using, aiming raised in first person), sword (no states), staff (charging mode); all textures pass the texture checks and quality bar.

### 4. Plugin side (`lib/cyrus/designer`)
`ItemDesign.states?: { modes?: [{value, ability, during}], flags?: [{name, ability, during}], aim?: {animation?} }`, `during` = `cooldown` | `no_charges` | `charging`. Checks: unresolved ability, `no_charges` without charges, `charging` without charge_release, `aim` on a base with its own use (bow, crossbow, trident, shield, spyglass, goat horn, brush, rods, food/potions) or with item_consume (errors); cooldown without cooldownTicks, states without a model, a mode/flag the item model has no state for, aim without a using state (warnings); 1.21.1: states ignored with a warning and a README note. Compiler: a 18th component `designer/ModelStates.java` is emitted ONLY when a design has states (1.21.4+), so every existing designer mod keeps its bytes and the 17-component library hash: a 2-tick main-thread timer sets custom_model_data on design items in hands (`setStrings([mode])` for the first active mode, `setFlags` by index, component removed when nothing is active), aimable items get `minecraft:consumable` (3600 s, no sound `minecraft:intentionally_empty`, no particles) after `setItemMeta`, and `PlayerItemConsumeEvent` is cancelled for them (the one cancel in a designer mod). Flag indexes follow the item model spec when the service passes it (`assets.itemModels`), else declaration order; the portal re-compile gets the same map from `designCompile.itemModels`. A custom bow = base `minecraft:bow` + `assets.model` (real bow behaviour drives the pull states; no extra code).

### 5. Studio preview (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel/preview.ts`, `TextureStudio.tsx`)
Live preview tab "In hand" is now **"In game"** with a context row (Hotbar, Dropped, First person, Third person, Item frame, Head) using the computed display transforms, and a **State** scrubber (Idle, Pull 1-3, Aim, Reload...) that swaps in each state's texture and display; opening a state texture selects its state. The view's `itemModels` come from the asset rows. Without a spec the derived default (tool / gun) is exactly the old in-hand scene (test). Cameras, slot, frame, ground shadow and the head-layer offset are Cyrus's approximation: the panel keeps the **approximate** label. Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/itemstates-*.png` (13, Playwright on devhost, fixtures in `scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` for the top-plan account; `test/e2e/cyrus-itemstates.shots.mjs`). The existing shots script now clicks "In game".

### 6. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`itemmodel/route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts` after the plan): flag on + textures allowed + 1.21.4+ + state words (bow, crossbow, gun, pistol, rifle, aim, reload, pull back, item frame, on the head, first person...), `assets.itemmodel` explicit, or a base that has specs -> `service.itemmodel = true`, `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.itemStates = { route, matched }`.
- **Service**: `assets.itemmodel` parsed (non-boolean 400; off with a note when textures are off); `ITEM MODEL STATES` section only when routed (examples generated from the templates, `itemmodel-example.json`), assets line in the user turn; allow-list `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`; specs kept byte for byte on a change build without the route; `itemmodels.js` validates with the GENERATED `itemmodel-spec.js` against the surviving textures inside the shared asset round (bounded repairs; a spec that keeps failing, or whose texture was dropped, is dropped as kind `itemmodel` and the item keeps one look); `assetResult.itemModels` + `itemModelPromptVersion` `mb-itemmodel-2026-10-10.1`; designs get the needs map; `/health` lists `itemmodel`; Dockerfile copies `itemmodels.js`, `itemmodel-spec.js`, `itemmodel-example.json`.
- **Portal sync** (`itemmodel/sync.ts` + `assets/sync.ts`): every returned spec re-validated against the textures that passed the portal's own checks; the valid ones go into `buildPack`; manifest `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`, one asset row per spec, `MbAssets.itemModels`; idempotent like the other assets.
- Generated files: `scripts/cyrus/build-itemmodel-artifacts.ts` (bundle + JSON Schema + prompt example; a test fails when stale), `scripts/cyrus/itemmodel-golden.ts --write`.

### 7. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-itemmodel.test.ts` 32/32 (caps at the edge, semantic codes, needs, display = vanilla numbers, vanilla bow byte-identical, crossbow canonical hashes + evaluator, layer order + scrubber inputs, goldens, determinism, byte-identical packs, bow/gun pack contents, 1.21.1 refusal, designer states validation / ModelStates only with states / flag indexes / no reflection-threads-network, TS == generated JS, artifacts current, service checker, request parser, prompt, preview scenes, router, build request, portal sync idempotency); `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` +3 (routed build returns specs with needs; missing-texture repair then ships; dead spec dropped with textures still shipping; not routed = file removed, 400, /health). Full-suite numbers: see the merge note below.
- RAN REAL on node-2 (`devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-itemmodel-real.ts --out ...`, raw `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/itemstates-r10-flights-2026-10-10.json`): javac 28 sources, 0 warnings on 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25); reproducible jars; strict scan 0 blocks / 0 warnings; **Test Flight passed on Paper 1.21.11 (b132) and 26.2**: plugin enabled, `list` identity=ok for the gun / bow / staff, the ModelStates self-check logged `mode reloading=ok cleared=ok aim=ok` (pistol) and `mode charging=ok cleared=ok` (staff) with the real component string (`minecraft:custom_model_data={strings: ["reloading"]}`, `minecraft:consumable={animation: "bow", consume_seconds: 3600.0f, has_consume_particles: 0b, sound: "minecraft:intentionally_empty"}`, `minecraft:item_model=...`); vanilla round trip through RCON (`item replace` into a chest + `data get`) stores the same strings / flags `[1b, 0b]` / consumable values; no ERROR line from the plugin; no leftovers.
- **NOT RUN / UNVERIFIED**: no real Minecraft client: **how the items LOOK and switch in a client is unverified** (display transforms, pull stages, the gun aim pose and slowdown, hand bob, the head / frame / ground placements); no player, so no item was really given to a player (the self-check builds the stack the give command would give); 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 26.1.2 not javac'd (no classpath; ItemUseAnimation names on 1.21.4 Paper unverified); no real model build; nothing deployed.

### 8. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- The spec's `name` must be its idle texture (so `setItemModel` / `assets.model` keys stay what they were); state models live under `models/item/<name>/` (no clash with texture names).
- A fixed layer priority (broken > damage > mode > flag > charged > using/pull > selected > context) instead of free boolean expressions: no duplicated subtrees, bounded size, matches vanilla's crossbow order on 1.21.11+.
- Plugin "mode" = custom_model_data `strings[0]` (one at a time), "flags" = `flags[]`; floats / colors not exposed.
- All 8 display contexts written explicitly; `on_shelf` and 26.x `transformation` not emitted; parent `item/generated`.
- Gun aiming = a never-finishing consumable (1 h, silent, cancelled if it ever finishes) with the `bow` pose by default; aim refused on bases with their own use. The consumable uses Paper's experimental data component API on 1.21.x (the only experimental use; stated in the component metadata).
- ModelStates refreshes every 2 ticks for items in hands only (items elsewhere keep their last state until held); no Tasks change (keeps old goldens).
- Studio tab renamed "In hand" -> "In game"; contexts in a row above the stage, the scrubber below it.

### 9. Owner actions (nothing needed to merge)
1. Decide whether to switch `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES=1` after a real-client check. 2. Real-client test day: bow pull stages, gun aim + reload look, head / frame / dropped placements, hand bob, the handgun rotations, on 1.21.11 and 26.x. 3. Rebuild the build-service image with the three new files. 4. Optional: re-check the registry's `dataComponentsStable` (26.2's Paper no longer marks the API experimental). 5. Cleanup: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-r10-itemstates` (tokens, shots, results).
EOF

- **Vanilla bow** (`items/bow.json`, byte-identical on 1.21.4 / 1.21.11 / 26.2, sha256 `65ccad78...`): condition `minecraft:using_item` -> on_true range_dispatch `minecraft:use_duration` scale `0.05`, entries `bow_pulling_1` at `0.65`, `bow_pulling_2` at `0.9`, fallback `bow_pulling_0`; on_false `item/bow`. Cyrus's emitter given the vanilla states produces the SAME BYTES (test).
- **Vanilla crossbow**: 1.21.4 = condition using_item { on_true range_dispatch `minecraft:crossbow/pull` entries 0.58 / 1.0 fallback pulling_0; on_false select `minecraft:charge_type` cases `arrow` / `rocket` fallback crossbow }. **1.21.11 and 26.2 swap the two outer layers** (select charge_type outermost, condition using_item in its fallback). Cyrus's order equals 1.21.11 / 26.2 by canonical hash; the 1.21.4 order is the swap (canonical hash checked) and the evaluator shows both pick the same model for every reachable input (a charged crossbow is never "used").
- **Model display defaults**: `item/generated` ground [0,0,0]/[0,2,0]/0.5, head [0,180,0]/[0,13,7]/1, thirdperson_righthand [0,0,0]/[0,3,1]/0.55, firstperson_righthand [0,-90,25]/[1.13,3.2,1.13]/0.68, fixed [0,180,0]/-/1; `item/handheld` the four hands as before; `item/bow` thirdperson_righthand [-80,260,-40]/[-1,-2,2.5]/0.9, lefthand [-80,-280,40], firstperson [0,-90,25] / [0,90,-25]; `item/crossbow` thirdperson [-90,0,-60] / [-90,0,30] at [2,0.1,-3]/0.9, firstperson [-90,0,-55] / [-90,0,35]. generated / handheld / bow / crossbow / bow_pulling_* / crossbow_pulling_* are identical (canonical) on 1.21.4, 1.21.11 and 26.2.
- **Components** (`CustomModelData` codec): `floats`, `flags`, `strings`, `colors`. `Consumable`: `consume_seconds`, `animation`, `sound`, `has_consume_particles`, `on_consume_effects`. `ItemUseAnimation`: 1.21.4 none/eat/drink/block/bow/spear/crossbow/spyglass/toot_horn/brush/bundle; 26.2 adds `trident` (and keeps `spear` for the new spear): Cyrus only offers bow / crossbow / spyglass / none.
- **Paper API** (javap, both lanes): `ItemMeta#getCustomModelDataComponent / setCustomModelDataComponent / hasCustomModelDataComponent / getAsComponentString`, `CustomModelDataComponent#get/setFlags(List<Boolean>) / get/setStrings(List<String>)` (stable Bukkit API); `DataComponentTypes.CONSUMABLE`, `Consumable.consumable()` builder (`consumeSeconds(float)`, `animation`, `sound(Key)`, `hasConsumeParticles`), `ItemUseAnimation.{NONE,BOW,CROSSBOW,SPYGLASS,...}`, `ItemStack#setData/hasData`. `DataComponentTypes` is `@ApiStatus.Experimental` on 1.21.11 and `@MinecraftVersionDependent` (not experimental) on 26.2; the registry's `dataComponentsStable` capability is only on 26.3 (left unchanged; worth re-checking).

### 2. ItemModelSpec v1 (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel/spec.ts`, `itemmodel.v1.schema.json`)
One file per stateful item, `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`, at most 12 per mod, 16 KB each: `{ schemaVersion: 1, name, category, display?, states?: [{ id, label?, texture, when, display? }], handAnimationOnSwap? }`. `name` = the idle texture's name = the item model key (`<ns>:<name>`, what `setItemModel` / the design's `assets.model` already point at). Categories (display defaults, `display.ts`): sword / tool / wand = vanilla handheld, bow = vanilla bow, crossbow = vanilla crossbow, flat / shield = vanilla generated, gun = the existing Cyrus handgun rotations re-gripped on the idle pixels. `display` overrides any context and field (owner/studio), per state too; all 8 contexts are always written explicitly (a missing left hand = the right hand, like the deserializer).
**Conditions** (closed set; layer order outermost first, first match wins): `broken` -> `damage {from}` (range_dispatch damage, normalised) -> `mode {value}` (select custom_model_data strings[0]) -> `flag {name}` (condition custom_model_data flags[i], i = declaration order) -> `charged {charge}` (crossbow only) -> `using` | `pull {from, source?}` (using_item + range_dispatch use_duration scale 0.05, or crossbow/pull) -> `selected` -> `context {contexts}` (select display_context) -> idle. **Caps**: 8 states, 9 textures, 4 pull stages (exactly one from 0), 6 modes, 4 flags, 4 damage stages, 3 context states, rotation +-360, translation +-80, scale +-4, pull from 0-100. Codes: reserved_id, dup_state, using_and_pull, pull_no_start, pull_mixed, crossbow_only, crossbow_range, dup_mode/flag/damage/charged/using/selected/broken, too_many_*, context_overlap, context_all, texture_unknown, version, too_big; warning use_needs_usable_base. **Versions**: 1.21.4+ (registry `itemModelDefinitions`); 1.21.1 refused with the registry's message. **The legacy predicate / overrides emitter for 1.21.1 is OUT of scope.**

### 3. Generator + pack (`emit.ts`, `templates.ts`, `lib/cyrus/textures/pack.ts`)
`emitItemModel(spec, {namespace, version, textures?, idle?})` -> `assets/<ns>/items/<name>.json` (vanilla key order: type first, then alphabetical; 2-space JSON), `models/item/<name>.json` (idle) and `models/item/<name>/<state>.json` (parent `minecraft:item/generated`, `layer0` = the state's texture, full display). `hand_animation_on_swap: false` when plugin-set states exist (a custom_model_data change would bob the hand). Same bytes on every version family (golden hashes for bow / gun / sword / staff on 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2). `buildPack({..., itemModels})`: textures covered by a spec get the spec's files instead of the flat default; **no specs = byte-identical packs** (sha1 compared with pack.ts at 5aa6fe5e52). `evalNode` / `resolveState` / `inputForState`: a TS evaluator of definitions (ours or vanilla's) for tests and the studio. Templates: bow (idle + pulling_0/1/2 at 0 / 0.65 / 0.9), gun (reloading mode > aiming using, aiming raised in first person), sword (no states), staff (charging mode); all textures pass the texture checks and quality bar.

### 4. Plugin side (`lib/cyrus/designer`)
`ItemDesign.states?: { modes?: [{value, ability, during}], flags?: [{name, ability, during}], aim?: {animation?} }`, `during` = `cooldown` | `no_charges` | `charging`. Checks: unresolved ability, `no_charges` without charges, `charging` without charge_release, `aim` on a base with its own use (bow, crossbow, trident, shield, spyglass, goat horn, brush, rods, food/potions) or with item_consume (errors); cooldown without cooldownTicks, states without a model, a mode/flag the item model has no state for, aim without a using state (warnings); 1.21.1: states ignored with a warning and a README note. Compiler: a 18th component `designer/ModelStates.java` is emitted ONLY when a design has states (1.21.4+), so every existing designer mod keeps its bytes and the 17-component library hash: a 2-tick main-thread timer sets custom_model_data on design items in hands (`setStrings([mode])` for the first active mode, `setFlags` by index, component removed when nothing is active), aimable items get `minecraft:consumable` (3600 s, no sound `minecraft:intentionally_empty`, no particles) after `setItemMeta`, and `PlayerItemConsumeEvent` is cancelled for them (the one cancel in a designer mod). Flag indexes follow the item model spec when the service passes it (`assets.itemModels`), else declaration order; the portal re-compile gets the same map from `designCompile.itemModels`. A custom bow = base `minecraft:bow` + `assets.model` (real bow behaviour drives the pull states; no extra code).

### 5. Studio preview (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel/preview.ts`, `TextureStudio.tsx`)
Live preview tab "In hand" is now **"In game"** with a context row (Hotbar, Dropped, First person, Third person, Item frame, Head) using the computed display transforms, and a **State** scrubber (Idle, Pull 1-3, Aim, Reload...) that swaps in each state's texture and display; opening a state texture selects its state. The view's `itemModels` come from the asset rows. Without a spec the derived default (tool / gun) is exactly the old in-hand scene (test). Cameras, slot, frame, ground shadow and the head-layer offset are Cyrus's approximation: the panel keeps the **approximate** label. Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/itemstates-*.png` (13, Playwright on devhost, fixtures in `scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` for the top-plan account; `test/e2e/cyrus-itemstates.shots.mjs`). The existing shots script now clicks "In game".

### 6. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`itemmodel/route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts` after the plan): flag on + textures allowed + 1.21.4+ + state words (bow, crossbow, gun, pistol, rifle, aim, reload, pull back, item frame, on the head, first person...), `assets.itemmodel` explicit, or a base that has specs -> `service.itemmodel = true`, `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.itemStates = { route, matched }`.
- **Service**: `assets.itemmodel` parsed (non-boolean 400; off with a note when textures are off); `ITEM MODEL STATES` section only when routed (examples generated from the templates, `itemmodel-example.json`), assets line in the user turn; allow-list `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`; specs kept byte for byte on a change build without the route; `itemmodels.js` validates with the GENERATED `itemmodel-spec.js` against the surviving textures inside the shared asset round (bounded repairs; a spec that keeps failing, or whose texture was dropped, is dropped as kind `itemmodel` and the item keeps one look); `assetResult.itemModels` + `itemModelPromptVersion` `mb-itemmodel-2026-10-10.1`; designs get the needs map; `/health` lists `itemmodel`; Dockerfile copies `itemmodels.js`, `itemmodel-spec.js`, `itemmodel-example.json`.
- **Portal sync** (`itemmodel/sync.ts` + `assets/sync.ts`): every returned spec re-validated against the textures that passed the portal's own checks; the valid ones go into `buildPack`; manifest `assets/itemmodels/<name>.json`, one asset row per spec, `MbAssets.itemModels`; idempotent like the other assets.
- Generated files: `scripts/cyrus/build-itemmodel-artifacts.ts` (bundle + JSON Schema + prompt example; a test fails when stale), `scripts/cyrus/itemmodel-golden.ts --write`.

### 7. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-itemmodel.test.ts` 32/32 (caps at the edge, semantic codes, needs, display = vanilla numbers, vanilla bow byte-identical, crossbow canonical hashes + evaluator, layer order + scrubber inputs, goldens, determinism, byte-identical packs, bow/gun pack contents, 1.21.1 refusal, designer states validation / ModelStates only with states / flag indexes / no reflection-threads-network, TS == generated JS, artifacts current, service checker, request parser, prompt, preview scenes, router, build request, portal sync idempotency); `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` +3 (routed build returns specs with needs; missing-texture repair then ships; dead spec dropped with textures still shipping; not routed = file removed, 400, /health). Full-suite numbers: see the merge note below.
- RAN REAL on node-2 (`devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-itemmodel-real.ts --out ...`, raw `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/itemstates-r10-flights-2026-10-10.json`): javac 28 sources, 0 warnings on 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25); reproducible jars; strict scan 0 blocks / 0 warnings; **Test Flight passed on Paper 1.21.11 (b132) and 26.2**: plugin enabled, `list` identity=ok for the gun / bow / staff, the ModelStates self-check logged `mode reloading=ok cleared=ok aim=ok` (pistol) and `mode charging=ok cleared=ok` (staff) with the real component string (`minecraft:custom_model_data={strings: ["reloading"]}`, `minecraft:consumable={animation: "bow", consume_seconds: 3600.0f, has_consume_particles: 0b, sound: "minecraft:intentionally_empty"}`, `minecraft:item_model=...`); vanilla round trip through RCON (`item replace` into a chest + `data get`) stores the same strings / flags `[1b, 0b]` / consumable values; no ERROR line from the plugin; no leftovers.
- **NOT RUN / UNVERIFIED**: no real Minecraft client: **how the items LOOK and switch in a client is unverified** (display transforms, pull stages, the gun aim pose and slowdown, hand bob, the head / frame / ground placements); no player, so no item was really given to a player (the self-check builds the stack the give command would give); 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 26.1.2 not javac'd (no classpath; ItemUseAnimation names on 1.21.4 Paper unverified); no real model build; nothing deployed.

### 8. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- The spec's `name` must be its idle texture (so `setItemModel` / `assets.model` keys stay what they were); state models live under `models/item/<name>/` (no clash with texture names).
- A fixed layer priority (broken > damage > mode > flag > charged > using/pull > selected > context) instead of free boolean expressions: no duplicated subtrees, bounded size, matches vanilla's crossbow order on 1.21.11+.
- Plugin "mode" = custom_model_data `strings[0]` (one at a time), "flags" = `flags[]`; floats / colors not exposed.
- All 8 display contexts written explicitly; `on_shelf` and 26.x `transformation` not emitted; parent `item/generated`.
- Gun aiming = a never-finishing consumable (1 h, silent, cancelled if it ever finishes) with the `bow` pose by default; aim refused on bases with their own use. The consumable uses Paper's experimental data component API on 1.21.x (the only experimental use; stated in the component metadata).
- ModelStates refreshes every 2 ticks for items in hands only (items elsewhere keep their last state until held); no Tasks change (keeps old goldens).
- Studio tab renamed "In hand" -> "In game"; contexts in a row above the stage, the scrubber below it.

### 9. Owner actions (nothing needed to merge)
1. Decide whether to switch `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES=1` after a real-client check. 2. Real-client test day: bow pull stages, gun aim + reload look, head / frame / dropped placements, hand bob, the handgun rotations, on 1.21.11 and 26.x. 3. Rebuild the build-service image with the three new files. 4. Optional: re-check the registry's `dataComponentsStable` (26.2's Paper no longer marks the API experimental). 5. Cleanup: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-r10-itemstates` (tokens, shots, results).

input.message:
Item model states and display contexts are built on `feature/cyrus-r10` and committed. tsc is clean, and the full Cyrus + modbuilder suite passes 1429/1429 after merging the latest `feature/cyrus-r2`. Nothing is deployed and the flag `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES` is off.

**What I built** (`lib/cyrus/itemmodel/`):
- **Spec** (`spec.ts`, JSON Schema in sync): 8 display contexts with defaults per category, owner overrides, a closed set of state conditions, strict caps. 1.21.1 is refused with the registry's message.
- **Generator** (`emit.ts`, `display.ts`): golden-tested bow, gun, sword and staff templates (`templates.ts`). Packs with no states stay byte-identical to the old pack builder.
- **Plugin side**: `ItemDesign.states`, plus a new `ModelStates.java` component that is only emitted when a design uses states, so existing designer mods keep their exact bytes.
- **Studio**: the "In hand" tab is now "In game", with a 6-view context switcher and a state scrubber; it still says "approximate".
- **Service, router, portal sync**: wired through all the shared files, with a generated JS validator tested equal to the TypeScript one.

**Ran:**
- Pure tests (32), 3 new pipeline tests with the fake CLI, a DB sync idempotency test, designer goldens.
- Node-2 flights on 1.21.11 and 26.2: javac 0 warnings, strict scan 0 findings, Test Flight passed on both.
- The plugin's self-check confirmed the state value and the aim component are really set on an item it built and cleared afterwards. Vanilla accepted the same values through RCON.
- 13 Playwright screenshots in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/itemstates-*.png`; I looked at them.
- Flight results: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/itemstates-r10-flights-2026-10-10.json`.

**Not run:**
- No game client, so how items look and switch in game is unverified.
- No player, so nothing was really given to a player.
- No javac on 1.21.4, 1.21.8 or 26.1.2.
- No real model build.

**Vanilla format facts** (from the asset mirror and Mojang's client jars):
- Bow: `using_item` condition, then `use_duration` with scale 0.05 and thresholds 0.65 / 0.9. My emitter reproduces vanilla's `bow.json` byte for byte; the file is identical on 1.21.4, 1.21.11 and 26.2.
- Crossbow: `crossbow/pull` 0.58 / 1.0 plus `charge_type`. 1.21.11 swapped the outer layers compared with 1.21.4.
- Custom model data properties read by `index`. The `on_shelf` context exists from 1.21.9.
- 26.x adds an optional `transformation` field, which I don't emit.
- Paper's data-component API is marked experimental on 1.21.11 but not on 26.2. The registry's `dataComponentsStable` capability is only set on 26.3; I left it unchanged.

**Merge:** feature/cyrus-r2 brought in R4 worldgen. I kept both sides in every conflict, regenerated the bundles, and the two /health tests now expect `itemmodel` in the feature list.

**Decisions the plan didn't specify:**
- The spec's name must be its idle texture's name.
- Conditions follow a fixed priority: broken, damage, mode, flag, charged, using/pull, selected, context, idle.
- Plugin "mode" is a single string (`strings[0]`); flags are separate.
- Gun aim is a silent, never-finishing consumable; its consume event is cancelled.
- Held items refresh every 2 ticks.
- The studio tab was renamed "In hand" → "In game".

The legacy emitter for 1.21.1 is out of scope.
